correctness.rationale: For ideal Mogi surface displacement μ=A(x−X,y−Y,d)/[(x−X)²+(y−Y)²+d²]^(3/2), local 4-vector parameters (A,d,X,Y) and n≥3 full three-component isotropic iid Gaussian observations on one common radius r, explicit differentiated Jacobian columns yield FIM. Angular rotation conjugates parameter X,Y block, and strict concavity logdet bounds any FIM by group average. Equality iff FIM itself invariant, equivalent to vanishing first and second complex angular sums; regular n-gon reaches it for all n≥3. Balanced determinant is (n⁴ A⁶/σ⁸) r²(d²+(5/2)r²)²/(r²+d²)^14, positive for r,d,A>0. With z=r²/d², derivative of z(1+5z/2)²/(1+z)^14 =−(5z+2)(55z²+11z−2)/(4(1+z)^15), unique positive maximizer z=(sqrt(561)−11)/110; zero at endpoints guarantees global radius optimality. Independently computed full Fisher blocks and determinant in exact SymPy arithmetic and checked unbalanced angular strict loss and derivative root.
residual_risks: Local common-radius design only; depends on a correct ideal point-source model, positive depth and amplitude, equal iid isotropic full-vector noise.
Not an optimal design among stations at different radii or a deployment recommendation under real topography/heteroscedasticity.

value.rationale: The theorem solves an entire natural restricted experiment-design family: how to position n full-vector GNSS stations on a common ring while estimating both source strength, depth and horizontal position. Exact moment conditions plus universal depth-scaled radius form a reproducible benchmark for simulation and design comparison, without claiming real-world optimal monitoring.
residual_risks: Model uncertainty, correlated or anisotropic errors and mixed radius stations can shift optimum.
